headline: Threats prompt tighter security at Chinese and Japanese embassies in Dhaka
summary: Police hold emergency meetings with ambassadors after an email threatening to attack the Chinese mission, purportedly from an extremist group.
details: Police officials held separate meetings with the Chinese and Japanese ambassadors in Dhaka on Friday to discuss security following threats against the embassies.
An email threatening to attack the Chinese embassy, purportedly sent in the name of an extremist organisation, was received on Thursday night.
The embassy informed Police Headquarters and the Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit, prompting immediate action.
CTTC Joint Commissioner Munshi Shahabuddin led meetings with Chinese Ambassador Yao Wen and Japanese Ambassador Saida Shinichi in Baridhara.
Additional Deputy Commissioner Mohammad Abu Khayer stated that authorities are verifying the source of the email and strengthening existing security measures.
A CTTC official suggested the email may have been a hoax, though an investigation and security sweep of the area are underway.
The incident occurs amid heightened concern among law enforcement agencies following several recent reports of bomb-like objects found in Dhaka and other parts of the country.
caption:
An email from a purported extremist group threatening the Chinese embassy has put Dhaka's diplomatic zone on high alert.

Police officials held separate meetings with the Chinese and Japanese ambassadors in Dhaka on Friday to discuss security following threats against the embassies.

An email threatening to attack the Chinese embassy, purportedly sent in the name of an extremist organisation, was received on Thursday night.

The embassy informed Police Headquarters and the Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit, prompting immediate action.

CTTC Joint Commissioner Munshi Shahabuddin led meetings with Chinese Ambassador Yao Wen and Japanese Ambassador Saida Shinichi in Baridhara.

Additional Deputy Commissioner Mohammad Abu Khayer stated that authorities are verifying the source of the email and strengthening existing security measures.

A CTTC official suggested the email may have been a hoax, though an investigation and security sweep of the area are underway.

The incident occurs amid heightened concern among law enforcement agencies following several recent reports of bomb-like objects found in Dhaka and other parts of the country.

Source: Jamuna TV, The Daily Star

headline_marked: 4 killed in Rangpur: [[Retired teacher and family murdered]] in suspected robbery
headline: 4 killed in Rangpur: Retired teacher and family murdered in suspected robbery
summary: The victims include a retired teacher of Rangpur Zilla School, his wife, and their two children, found dead in their three-story building.
details: The bodies of retired teacher Ganapati Chakraborty, his wife, and their two children were recovered from their three-story building in Kamal Kachna Machhuapara village, Rangpur city.
Local residents and police discovered the bodies on Saturday night around 8:30 PM.
According to the CID, the victims were strangled with ropes or towels approximately 3-4 days before the discovery.
Investigators found that the electrical connection to the building had been disconnected and the area where money was kept had been broken into, suggesting a robbery occurred.
caption:
A retired teacher, his wife, and two children found dead in Rangpur. A suspected robbery turned into a mass murder.

The bodies of retired teacher Ganapati Chakraborty, his wife, and their two children were recovered from their three-story building in Kamal Kachna Machhuapara village, Rangpur city.

Local residents and police discovered the bodies on Saturday night around 8:30 PM.

According to the CID, the victims were strangled with ropes or towels approximately 3-4 days before the discovery.

Investigators found that the electrical connection to the building had been disconnected and the area where money was kept had been broken into, suggesting a robbery occurred.

#Rangpur #CrimeNews #Bangladesh #Justice #Tragedy

Source: Prothom Alo
